response.consequence: Legacy storage writes can fail with `context canceled`, or can be skipped. Legacy storage then silently diverges from unified storage, even though Mode 3 is meant to keep writing to both. The failures are recorded only as legacy error metrics.
response.explanation: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection now run the legacy write in a goroutine. Each goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. The handler returns right after starting the goroutine, so the request context is cancelled and the derived context is cancelled with it. The legacy call then runs with an already-cancelled or soon-cancelled context. The goroutine also uses `obj`, `objInfo` and `options` after the handler has returned, so the caller may still be mutating them.
